title: Collapsible Trait Hierarchies
pattern: A trait hierarchy where the trait and its single implementer are identical, with no alternative implementations or polymorphic calls.
why_bad: Unnecessary indirection. Multiple levels of abstraction with no polymorphism add cognitive noise and slow down code navigation.
detection: A trait with exactly one implementer whose methods are exactly identical to the trait definitions, with no polymorphic usage.
counterexample: Explicit boundaries between packages to isolate unstable third-party code, or testing boundaries for complex IO.
fix: Apply Collapse Hierarchy: remove the trait and let consumers use the concrete struct directly.
